title: Tiles-first Activity Hub + Contextual Top Navigation for Console (dashboards, rollouts, cost views)
creator: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:
The Console's current left-rail and route-first patterns make it hard for users to discover high-value operational surfaces (dashboards, live rollouts, and cost breakdowns) in context. This ticket proposes a tiles-first Activity Hub placed in the top navigation as a contextual entrypoint. The hub surfaces role-relevant quick tiles (e.g., Live Rollouts, Cost Snapshot, Token Usage, Alerts) and maps into router states for direct landing pages.

Goals:
- Improve discoverability of operational surfaces without inflating left-rail complexity.
- Reduce time-to-insight for common tasks (viewing rollout status, checking cost anomalies, opening a model dashboard).
- Maintain consistent workspace-scoped routing and keyboard-first switching.
- Make the hub extensible so product teams can add tiles (e.g., Billing, Dedicated capacity metrics) without changing IA.

Proposed solution (high level):
1) Top-right contextual activity button (sparkline + count) toggles the Activity Hub overlay anchored to the top nav.
2) Default hub shows 8–12 tiles grouped by: Observability, Rollouts, Costs, Shortcuts. Each tile has a primary action and a secondary quick action (e.g., "Open dashboard" and "Create alert").
3) Tiles deep-link to console routes with an optional query param for 'entry=hub' to enable micro-onboarding banners and commit telemetry.
4) Workspace switch lives adjacent to the hub pill; switching still updates the global route but also reorders hub tiles based on workspace intent.
5) Keyboard: Cmd/Ctrl+K opens command palette; T (when palette is open) jumps to hub tiles; arrow keys navigate tiles; Enter opens.

Architectural notes for the router: 
- Use route fragments /dashboard/:id?entry=hub and /rollouts/:id?entry=hub so analytics can attribute discovery.
- Keep left-rail as persistent route map, but collapse low-usage items into "More" to avoid nav duplication.

Prototype artifacts: 
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/Redwood/console-activity-hub-proto (see pages: Hub-v1, Hub-v2 with emphasis on costs)
- Miro exploration: https://miro.com/app/board/uX_example_board
- Clickable prototype (InVision): https://inv.redwood.ai/proto/ActivityHub-v1

Acceptance criteria:
- Design spec with responsive layouts for 1200px / 1024px / 768px breakpoints present in Figma.
- Interactive prototype demonstrates keyboard flows and direct deep-links to: Rollouts list, Rollout detail, Cost Summary, Model Dashboard.
- Token-level telemetry hooks defined for: tile_seen, tile_click, tile_open_via_keyboard, hub_open (PRD instrumentation table attached).
- Accessibility: tiles meet 4.5:1 contrast, are focusable, have aria-labels, and can be used with screen readers.

Trade-offs considered:
- Option A: Expand left-rail with hierarchical groups (previous approach) — pros: discoverable; cons: permanent UI bloat, harder mobile mapping.
- Option B (this proposal): Top-nav hub — pros: reduces left-rail noise, atomic discoverability, easier to A/B test; cons: temporary overlay could be missed by some users, extra layer of routing complexity.

Metrics to evaluate success (30/60/90 days):
- Hub open rate (target 20% of active console sessions by day 30)
- Tile click-to-open conversion (target 25% for Rollouts and Cost Snapshot tiles)
- Reduction in left-rail clicks to reach Rollouts (target -30%)
- Time-to-first-insight for cost anomalies (target -20%)

Design notes / UI details:
- Tile sizes: primary grid 160x120 (desktop), compressed 120x88 (tablet).
- Visual tokens: use existing console color palette; costs tiles use amber+gradient to indicate spending urgency.
- Microcopy: each tile has short prefix (context) + one-line description + CTA. Example: "Costs
 Snapshot
 Estimated spend this month — View details"

Implementation considerations / handoff items:
- Needed frontend feature flags: feature.activity_hub, feature.hub_tile_customization.
- Backend: new endpoint for personalized tile ordering: GET /api/v1/users/:id/hub_tiles. ENG needs to add caching for 1s freshness.
- Instrumentation: add telemetry events described above (see links).

Next steps / rollout plan:
- Design: finalize high-fidelity screens and annotate interactions (due 2026-03-15).
- Research: short usability run (5 sessions) to validate discoverability and labeling (run 2026-03-16 to 2026-03-19).
- Engineering: spike for overlay performance & keyboard nav (ENG-2573).
- Launch: behind feature flag in console-2026.04, gradual nerd-sniffing to 10% then 50% before full rollout.

Note: This approach intentionally reframes discovery as a temporary context (hub) instead of expanding persistent nav, aiming to reduce cognitive load for new users while preserving route parity for power users.
comments: 2026-02-27 — Jonah Reeves (PM): Love the tiles-first idea; please add a horizontal compact variant for users who primarily use left-rail. Ask ENG about caching implications.
2026-03-02 — Priya Nair (Eng): Backend OK to add hub_tiles endpoint. Concern: frequent workspace switches may cause reordering churn; recommend sticky ordering per session with server override.
2026-03-05 — Sofia Lee (Design Review): Iterated colors for Cost tile to meet accessibility. Suggested adding small on-tile sparklines for usage signals.
2026-03-08 — QA: Flagged keyboard focus trap in overlay when going between iFrames — assigned to ENG-2678.
review_feedback: Decision 2026-03-09: Proceed with Top-nav Hub A11y-first variant. Keep left-rail unchanged except collapsing 'More' items.
PM asked to track hub->route bounce rates and include that in the rollout dashboard (see links).
Eng requested feature flagging for iterative rollout and a perf budget (overlay open < 120ms).
